name: Manor
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Manor, TX 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Manor, TX: Deck the Park tree lighting at Jennie Lane Park and Holidays in Manor with ice skating, rides and Santa.
lede: Manor's Christmas belongs to the city: a tree lighting called Deck the Park at Jennie Lane Park downtown, followed a week later by Holidays in Manor, a free afternoon with ice skating, rides and Santa out on US Highway 290.
celebrates: The City of Manor runs two holiday events that bookend early December. Deck the Park lights the city Christmas tree at Jennie Lane Park on East Rector Street with a countdown, caroling, holiday characters, hot cocoa and cookies. Holidays in Manor follows at the East Manor Development site on US Highway 290, where the city sets up ice skating, winter themed rides, crafts, games, food trucks, live music, local vendors and photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus. Both appear on the city's official list of special events, next to Movies in the Park and the 4th of July, and both are free.
lastyear: Manor held its first Deck the Park tree lighting at Jennie Lane Park in 2025, which is why the city calls the 2026 lighting the second annual, and the city streamed the 2025 lighting live on its Facebook page. The City of Manor then hosted Holidays in Manor on Saturday, December 6, 2025, at 15317 East US Highway 290. The city's event listing promised a country chic twist on the celebration that year.
facts: Manor is named for James Manor, who became postmaster when a post office called Grassdale opened here in 1859. A second post office, opened in 1871 as Gregg, was renamed Manor in 1872. The same year the Houston and Texas Central Railway laid its tracks through town, on right of way that a historical marker says James Manor donated in 1871. Manor incorporated in the early 1930s. Its Deck the Park tree lighting is one of the town's newest traditions.
trains: Manor is a railroad town: the Houston and Texas Central Railway built through it in 1871, on land James Manor gave for the right of way. Capital MetroRail's Red Line does not reach Manor; it runs between Downtown Austin and Leander. The closest Amtrak stops are the Austin station and the Taylor station, where the Texas Eagle stops, northeast of Manor. For a holiday train ride, the Austin Steam Train Association runs vintage trains from Cedar Park.
train_links: Vintage train rides from Cedar Park, including the Hill Country Flyer and the North Pole Flyer at Christmas.

kidfact: Manor is named after a man named James Manor. He ran the first post office and gave land so the railroad could build its tracks through town in 1871.
faq: Where is the Manor Christmas tree lighting?

Deck the Park happens at Jennie Lane Park, 104 East Rector Street, in downtown Manor. The City of Manor counts down to the moment the tree lights up, with caroling, holiday music, holiday characters, hot cocoa, coffee, cookies and a photobooth. The 2026 lighting is only the second, so the tradition is still new.

Holidays in Manor is a free city event at East Manor Development No. 1, 15317 East US Highway 290. The city lists ice skating, winter themed rides, holiday games, crafts, food trucks, live music, local vendors and photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus. In 2025 it was held on Saturday, December 6.

Yes. The City of Manor calls Holidays in Manor a free, family friendly event, and Deck the Park is an open community gathering in a city park with light refreshments. Food trucks and vendors at Holidays in Manor charge for what they sell.
How did Manor get its name?

The Texas State Historical Association says James Manor was postmaster of the Grassdale post office opened in 1859, and the Gregg post office of 1871 was renamed Manor in 1872. A historical marker says he donated right of way to the Houston and Texas Central Railway in 1871.
